chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Whether to study Schillinger and his work habits
summary: They discuss Eubie studying Schillinger, Whaley being told he did not need it, and his habit of never listening to other arrangers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. "Good Night, Angeline." Sissle was the lyric writer, he used to write all the lyrics and Eubie, he took that course -- what was the name of the course, you know. Sillinger and Sissle said, don't put none of that Sillinger in my music." (laughs)
Yeah, he went back to school to study Sillinger.
Yeah, and he didn't need that.
But he's always been trying to be very aggressive, you got to give him credit for that.
Just like I wanted to take it and the man, said you don't need it, as much harmony as you play.
I took it. I went down there and took it too. I got the books over here now. It's nice to know

Roger Sequel told me, I said I'm going to take up Sillinger. He said, man, you don't need it. You are writing all this music and you need some Sillinger. I said well, everybody else is taking and he said, they have no imagination. You see, one thing I did while I was in the theatre, like that, I would never listen to anybody else's arrangements, scared I'd put something in. Hear something about theirs. I'd sit up all night and write a number. I remember we had a show at the Lafayette Theatre and Carey was the producer and we had some comedians in the show and they wanted to take over the show.
